Are there API call limits?
Yes. These vary by plan type:
- **Free** plan - 1000 calls per workspace per month
- **Team** plan - 100,000 calls per workspace per month
- **Business** and **Enterprise** plans - Unlimited API calls (Still subject to other limits such as the rate limits discussed above)

title: Airtable API Key Replaced: Use a Personal Access Token
snippet:
The workspace that holds the base has a monthly API allowance: 1,000 calls on Free, 100,000 on Team, and no monthly cap on Business or Enterprise Scale, according to [Airtable's plan limits](https://support.airtable.com/articles/2277136852-airtable-plans-overview?ref=airtables.net). Separately, [the API rate limit](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/rate-limits?ref=airtables.net) is 5 requests per second per base. Personal access tokens are available on all plans, in the browser and the Mac and Windows apps. API calls to that base count toward its workspace's allowance, including its metadata requests and calls made by connected tools. [The monthly counter resets on the first day of the calendar month](https://support.airtable.com/articles/7735693959-managing-api-call-limits-in-airtable?ref=airtables.net); the owner of a Free workspace can inspect Workspace settings → Usage → Public API calls. General request patterns belong in the [API & tokens](https://airtables.net/tag/api/) section.

Before opening the token page, settle who connects. [Airtable's authentication reference](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/authentication?ref=airtables.net) reserves personal access tokens for "personal development, like building an integration for yourself, your client, or your company", and says that "Any integrations that allow other users to grant access to Airtable should use OAuth."
| Who connects | Credential | What changes for you |
|---|---|---|
| A script you run, or build for a client or your company | Personal access token | It acts as your account, limited by the scopes and bases you add |
| An app other people connect to their own Airtable accounts | OAuth | Each person grants access; register the integration on the [OAuth integrations page](https://airtable.com/create/oauth?ref=airtables.net) |
| Zapier | OAuth only | Tokens are not accepted; reconnect the Airtable account inside Zapier |
| Make | Airtable OAuth, or a token connection | Connection type "Airtable Token or Key" with token type "Personal Access Token" |
| An integration that must outlive one person's account, on Enterprise Scale | Service account token | An admin creates it; the account is not billed and cannot log in |

title: Managing API call limits in Airtable
snippet:
[Airtable enforces a rate limit of 5 requests per second](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/rate-limits) (per base) to ensure optimal user performance across all pricing tiers. Additionally, there is a limit of 50 requests per second for all traffic using personal access tokens from a given user or service account. If you exceed this rate, you will receive a 429 status code and must wait 30 seconds before subsequent requests will succeed. API integrations should pause and wait before retrying the API request—behavior handled automatically by the official [JavaScript client](https://github.com/Airtable/airtable.js)—with back-off and retry logic.

# Monthly call limits for Free and Team plans
- Free plan: 1000 API calls per month
- Team plan: 100000 API calls per month
Monthly calls for [Free and Team plans](https://airtable.com/pricing) are also limited to 5 requests per second rate limit.

Airtable's API call limits vary by plan:
- Free: 1,000 API calls per workspace per month. Once exceeded, a 30-day grace period begins.
- Team: 100,000 API calls per workspace per month. Once the limit is reached, API calls are throttled to 2 requests per second.
- Business / Enterprise Scale: No monthly call cap; rate limiting applies per base.

title: Airtable API Pricing 2026: Free vs. Paid Tiers Explained
snippet:
**Airtable API pricing** ties directly to your workspace plan. Each base gets a monthly limit of API calls, and you pay extra if you exceed it. You don’t pay per seat for API access—it’s baked into the plan. But the caps differ dramatically between Free, Plus, Pro, and Enterprise.

| Plan | Monthly API Calls per Base | Overage Cost (per 1,000 calls) | Key Workspace Additions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 1,200 | Hard cap (no overages) | Up to 1,200 records per base |
| Plus | 5,000 | $1.00 | 5 GB attachments, extensions |
| Pro | 50,000 | $0.50 | Scripting, advanced sync, 20 GB attachments |
| Enterprise | Custom | Negotiable | SSO, admin panel, dedicated support |

The free tier gives you the full API—no feature gaps. You can create, read, update, and delete records, work with attachments, and use all endpoints. The limitation is purely quantitative: 1,200 calls per base per month, plus a per-base record cap of 1,200.

Another hidden limitation: the Free plan blocks access to advanced sync features and extensions that help reduce API call count. So you end up writing more custom code, which ironically eats more resources.
